name: mod-blast-radius
description: Holds a risky Bash command (rm, git reset --hard, force push, SQL DROP and more) before it runs, shows what it would change, and lets you Run or Cancel

animations.title: Animations
animations.description: Entries shimmer while they wait. Hover colors also fade. Off, everything draws still

enabled.title: Hold risky commands
enabled.description: Risky Bash waits for your choice. You pick Run or Cancel. Off, every command runs as usual

explain.title: Explain with Haiku
explain.description: Each held command is sent to Haiku for a plain-language explanation on the card. It spends tokens. Off (the default), no model is called and the card shows the rule's reason and the preview

idle.title: Idle timeout
idle.description: A held command nobody answers for this long stops blocking Claude. The command does not run, Claude carries on and asks again after your next message, and a chip in the pill row keeps the command until you answer it. Off (the default), a card waits as long as it takes

onError.title: On check error
onError.description: What happens to a command when Blast radius cannot check it: a check that throws, or a rules.json that cannot be read. Hold (the default) holds it on the card, or asks the permission system where no card can draw. Run lets it through

recycle.title: Send rm to the bin
recycle.description: A plain rm whose every target is inside the session folder goes to the OS bin instead of deleting, and runs with no card. Windows uses the Recycle Bin through PowerShell, macOS uses trash or Finder, Linux uses gio trash. Where no bin is available the card holds it as before. Outside that folder only files this session made, that your keep file and mod-wrap-up do not keep, go to the bin too. Off (the default), an rm is held

alwaysCard.title: Always show the card
alwaysCard.description: A command judged risky but measured harmless (a file that does not exist, nothing to overwrite) passes silently. On, it still shows the card. Off (the default), it runs at once

icons.title: Icons
icons.description: auto picks Nerd Font or safe glyphs. It uses Nerd Font icons when the terminal's font is a Nerd Font (read from Windows Terminal, iTerm2, VS Code, Ghostty, kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, GNOME Terminal or Konsole) and safe Unicode glyphs elsewhere. nerd and safe force one
